rules.title: Structured Logging
rules.check: All logging must use structured logging with named parameters.
rules.rationale: Structured logs enable searching, filtering, and aggregation. They are machine-parseable and human-readable.

rules.title: Log Levels
rules.check: Log levels must be used consistently: Debug for development, Information for flow, Warning for recoverable issues, Error for failures.
rules.rationale: Consistent levels enable filtering and alerting. Misused levels create noise or miss important events.

rules.title: Correlation IDs
rules.check: All operations must have correlation IDs that propagate across service boundaries.
rules.rationale: Correlation enables tracing requests through distributed systems. Without correlation, debugging distributed issues is impractical.

rules.title: OpenTelemetry Tracing
rules.check: Services must implement distributed tracing using OpenTelemetry.
rules.rationale: OpenTelemetry is the standard for observability. It enables vendor-neutral tracing across services.

rules.title: Span Attributes
rules.check: Trace spans must include relevant attributes for debugging: operation type, entity IDs, result status.
rules.rationale: Rich span attributes enable filtering and analysis. They provide context for understanding trace behavior.

rules.title: Metrics Instrumentation
rules.check: Key operations must have metrics: counters for events, histograms for durations, gauges for state.
rules.rationale: Metrics enable alerting, capacity planning, and performance analysis. They provide quantitative system understanding.

rules.title: Exception Logging
rules.check: Exceptions must be logged with full stack trace at Error level. Caught exceptions must be logged at Warning.
rules.rationale: Complete exception information is essential for debugging. The level indicates whether the exception was handled.

rules.title: Performance Logging
rules.check: Operations exceeding performance thresholds must be logged with timing information.
rules.rationale: Performance anomalies must be detectable from logs. Threshold-based logging highlights issues without overwhelming logs.

rules.title: Health Check Details
rules.check: Health checks must report detailed status for each dependency.
rules.rationale: Aggregated health status is insufficient for debugging. Detailed checks identify the specific failing component.

rules.title: Log Context
rules.check: Logs must include request context: user ID (if authenticated), request path, operation name.
rules.rationale: Context enables filtering logs by user or operation. It provides the information needed to reproduce issues.

rules.title: Baggage Propagation
rules.check: OpenTelemetry Baggage MUST be used for cross-service context (tenant ID, feature flags).
rules.rationale: Baggage propagates context across service boundaries automatically. It enables consistent behavior in distributed systems.

rules.title: Metric Naming Convention
rules.check: Metrics MUST follow naming convention: {service}.{subsystem}.{metric} with units.
rules.rationale: Consistent naming enables dashboard templates and alerting rules. Units in names prevent interpretation errors.

rules.title: HTTP Handler Correlation
rules.check: All outgoing HTTP requests MUST include correlation headers via DelegatingHandler.
rules.rationale: Correlation headers enable distributed tracing across service boundaries.

rules.title: HTTP Request/Response Logging
rules.check: HTTP clients SHOULD log requests and responses via a logging handler for debugging.
rules.rationale: HTTP logging aids debugging integration issues without requiring external tools.

rules.title: Liveness Health Check Per Service
rules.check: Each service MUST have a dedicated liveness health check class.
rules.rationale: Liveness checks enable Kubernetes to detect hung processes. Each service should verify its critical dependencies.
